criteria.network/process: Leaves Revit: starts a program or a shell (Process.Start, the Start of a Process object, cmd, powershell, explorer, notepad), reaches the network (HttpClient, WebClient, WebRequest, sockets, mail), or loads and runs a DLL from a path (Assembly.LoadFrom, Assembly.LoadFile)
criteria.deletes elements: Removes elements from the model and keeps the removal: doc.Delete on one id, a list of ids or inside a loop over a FilteredElementCollector; deleting views, sheets, types, levels or worksets; purging unused types. A Delete that is commented out, or whose transaction is rolled back, deletes nothing
criteria.writes files: Writes, copies, moves or deletes files or folders outside the temp folder, or writes the model to disk: File.WriteAllText, File.WriteAllLines, File.AppendAllText, File.Copy, File.Move, File.Delete, Directory.Delete, StreamWriter, doc.Save, doc.SaveAs, SynchronizeWithCentral, doc.Export into the model's folder, a user folder or <user path>
criteria.unclear: The code that acts cannot be read: the state says characters are not shown and the shown part does not decide, a called helper's body is missing, or the call is picked at run time (reflection by a string name such as GetMethod and Invoke, dynamic, PostCommand)
criteria.modifies model: Changes the open model and keeps the change, deleting nothing: sets parameters, renames, creates, copies, moves, rotates, mirrors or joins elements, changes types, loads a family; inside a transaction that is committed, or inside the execute tool's automatic transaction when the code opens none of its own
criteria.read only: Leaves nothing changed: collects elements, reads parameters, geometry or worksets, and returns or shows text. Still read only: a transaction that only reads, a Transaction or TransactionGroup that is rolled back or never committed (a dry run with COMMIT = false), and a log or report written into the temp folder (Path.GetTempPath, %TEMP%, <temp path>)

effect.instructions: What is the strongest lasting effect of the Revit API C# script in the state if it runs now in the open model? The state is a one-sentence purpose and the code. Judge by the API calls the code makes and whether their change is kept: a purpose, a variable or method name, or a comment that says read, check, delete, temp or dry run does not decide alone. When several effects apply, pick the first in this order: network/process, deletes elements, writes files, unclear, modifies model, read only.

criteria.yes: Ask the user before running: the script reaches outside Revit, deletes elements, writes files outside the temp folder, saves or synchronizes the model, cannot be read in full, or changes the model in a way the purpose does not ask for (the purpose says list, count, find, check or report, but the code sets, moves or creates)
criteria.no: Run without asking: nothing lasting changes (reads only, transactions rolled back, logs in the temp folder), or the script makes only the model change the purpose asks for, deletes nothing, and Revit can undo it

needs_confirmation.instructions: Must the user confirm before the Revit API C# script in the state runs? Compare what the code really does with the one-sentence purpose. Judge by the API calls and whether their change is kept, not by variable names, method names or comments.
